{{Short description|None}}
Several notable opinion polls have been undertaken on [[Islam]] and related topics, including fundamentalism, and [[Islamic terrorism]]. Polls have interviewed both Muslim respondents and other groups.

==Countries==

===Australia===
*2005: In a 2005 [[Lowy Institute for International Policy]] Poll 57% of Australians indicated they are worried about the rise of Islamic fundamentalism.<ref>{{cite book |last=Guiora|first=Amos N. |title= 	Top Ten Global Justice Law Review Articles 2007|date=4 September 2008 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=JnHnCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA406|page=406|publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780195376586 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title= The Economist, Volume 375, Issues 8420-8428|year = 2005|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1ZvqAAAAMAAJ&q=57%25+australians+islamic+fundamentalism+united+states|page=58}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lowyinstitute.org/files/pubfiles/Australians_Speak_2005.pdf |title=The Lowy Institute Poll Australians Speak 2005 |access-date=2016-04-16 |archive-date=2016-04-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160424152706/http://www.lowyinstitute.org/files/pubfiles/Australians_Speak_2005.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>   [[Amos N. Guiora]] noted that this is equivalent to the number of Australians who perceived American Foreign Policy as a threat, he further noted that not just Muslim countries have an unfavourable opinion of the United States but a large number of western countries such as: France, Germany, Great Britain and Spain and concluded that Australia was not an outlier on this regard.<ref>{{cite book |last=Guiora|first=Amos N. |title=Top Ten Global Justice Law Review Articles 2007|date=4 September 2008 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=JnHnCwAAQBAJ&pg=PA406|page=406|publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780195376586 }}</ref> The Lowly Institute claimed that the result "raised eyebrows.<ref>[http://www.lowyinstitute.org/publications/lowy-institute-poll-2014 LOWY INSTITUTE POLL 2014]</ref> ''[[USA Today]]'' also analysed the data as showing that among Australians "57% judged U.S. foreign policy to be as much of a threat as Islamic fundamentalism", USA Today analysed the poll as having a margin of error of 3.1% <ref>[http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/news/world/2005-03-28-australia-us_x.htm Survey: Australians say U.S. policies as threatening as Islamic fundamentalism]</ref> ''[[The Economist]]'' claims [[Paul Keating]], Australia's former prime minister was “jolted” by the findings.<ref>[https://www.economist.com/asia/2005/03/31/new-best-friends New best friends Unwelcome news for Australia's Americophiles]</ref>

===Egypt===
*2011: In Egypt, a survey conducted by [[Pew Research]] found that 22% of Egyptians had confidence in [[Osama bin Laden]]. Dona J. Stewart, an External Research Associate at the [[Strategic Studies Institute]] analysed this as showing favorability for [[al-Qaeda]] on the decline in Egypt. To backup this claim she noted a 2006 survey which showed 27% of Egyptians had a favorable view of Bin Laden which went down to 22% in 2011.<ref>{{cite book |last=Stewart|first=Dona J.  |title=The Middle East Today: Political, Geographical and Cultural Perspectives|year=2013 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JYE2eOEmwmkC&pg=PA264|page=264|publisher=Routledge |isbn=9780415782432 }}</ref>
*2009: Research published in 2009 by WPO found that 44% of Egyptians had a favorable view of Osama Bin Laden, whereas 22% had a mixed view and 17% had a negative view.<ref name="Rane 182">{{cite book |last=Rane|first=Halim   |title=Islam and Contemporary Civilisation|year=2010 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iOHb6MCGuVQC&pg=PA182|page=182|publisher=Academic Monographs |isbn=9780522857283 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.worldpublicopinion.org/pipa/pdf/feb09/STARTII_Feb09_rpt.pdf |title=Public Opinion in the Islamic World on Terrorism, al Qaeda, and US Policies  |access-date=2016-04-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090306032425/http://www.worldpublicopinion.org/pipa/pdf/feb09/STARTII_Feb09_rpt.pdf |archive-date=2009-03-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Halim Rane]] Associate Professor at [[Griffith University]] analysed this data and others and concluded that research has shown that support for al-Qaeda and Bin Laden has generally declined over the decade.<ref name="Rane 182"/>

===Jordan===
*July 2005: 86% of Jordanian people when asked if [[Suicide bombings]] against Israelis were justifiable said they supported it, whereas 14% did not.  70% when asked if suicide bombings against Americans and Westerners in Iraq was justifies said "yes"<ref name="Hassan 123">{{cite book |last=Hassan |first=Riaz|title= Inside Muslim Minds|year=2008|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=Z4Ts0GkJBKgC&pg=PA123 |page=123|publisher=Melbourne Univ. |isbn=9780522854817}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=University |first=of Virginia|title= The Virginia Review of Asian Studies, Volume 8|year=2005|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=PupVAAAAYAAJ&q=65|page=65}}</ref><ref name="pewglobal.org">[http://www.pewglobal.org/2014/07/01/concerns-about-islamic-extremism-on-the-rise-in-middle-east/ Concerns about Islamic Extremism on the Rise in Middle East]</ref> The [[Free Republic]] analysed this as showing that the support for suicide bombings by Palestinian against Israelis was widespread however, they believe that the data as a whole shows that "there is broader agreement that suicide attacks in specific circumstances – against Americans and other Westerners in Iraq, and by Palestinians against Israeli citizens - are justified".<ref name="freerepublic.com">[http://www.freerepublic.com/focus/f-news/1444322/posts A Year After Iraq War (Pew Research Poll on Muslim attitudes shows high percentage favor terrorism)]</ref>

===Turkey===
*July 2005: 24% of Turkish people when asked if [[Suicide bombings]] against Israelis were justifiable said they supported it, whereas 67% did not.<ref name="Hassan 123"/><ref name="pewglobal.org"/> The ''[[LA Times]]'' analysed the entire PEW research poll from which this data came as showing support for terrorism being on the decline and support down since 2004.<ref>[https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2005-jul-15-fg-islam15-story.html Poll Finds Less Support for Terrorism]</ref> The [[Free Republic]] analysed this as showing that public opinion in Turkey for the support of Palestinian violence on the decline.<ref name="freerepublic.com"/>

===United Kingdom===
*August 2006:<ref name="Most People 'Threatened By Islam'">[http://news.sky.com/story/450258/most-people-threatened-by-islam Most People 'Threatened By Islam']</ref> A [[YouGov]] survey revealed that the number of Non Muslims who feel that "a large proportion of British Muslims feel no sense of loyalty to this country and are prepared to condone or even carry out acts of terrorism" was 10% after the [[7 July 2005 London bombings]], but had increased to 18% a year later in 2006.<ref>{{cite book |last=Communities and Local Government Committee |first=Parliament. House of Commons|title=Preventing Violent Extremism: Sixth Report of Session 2009-10 : Report ...|date=30 March 2010|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=XUdbVsADpfgC&pg=PA126 |page=126|publisher=The Stationery Office |isbn=9780215545466}}</ref><ref name="publications.parliament.uk">[https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm200809/cmselect/cmcomloc/memo/previoex/uc19a02.htm Supplementary memorandum from Institute for Policy Research & Development (PVE 19A)]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.secularism.org.uk/pollfindssuspicionofmuslimsincre.html |title=Poll Finds Suspicion Of Muslims Increasing |access-date=2016-04-16 |archive-date=2016-04-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160423172723/http://www.secularism.org.uk/pollfindssuspicionofmuslimsincre.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The  "Communities and Local GovernmentCommittee" of the British Parliament, [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] referred to this as disheartening/less heartening.<ref name="publications.parliament.uk"/><ref>{{cite book |last=Communities and Local Government Committee |first=Parliament. House of Commons|title=Preventing Violent Extremism: Sixth Report of Session 2009-10 : Report ...|date=30 March 2010|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=XUdbVsADpfgC&pg=PA126 |page=126|publisher=The Stationery Office |isbn=9780215545466}}</ref> [[Sky News]] analysed the entire data collected by [[YouGov]] (which included the data about loyalty) at that time as showing that a majority of people in Britain feel threatened by Islam.<ref name="Most People 'Threatened By Islam'"/>

===United States===
*August 2010: A ''[[New York Times]]'' poll found that 33% of Americans think that Muslim Americans were more "sympathetic to terrorists than other Citizens" [[Rik Coolsaet]] analysed this as indicating a high level of distrust directed at the American Muslim community.<ref>{{cite book |last=Coolsaet|first=Professor Dr Rik |title=Jihadi Terrorism and the Radicalisation Challenge: European and American ...|date=28 April 2013 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=GOKhAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA113 |page=113|publisher=Ashgate Publishing |isbn=9781409476450 }}</ref> New York Times did this survey during the [[Park51]] Ground Zero Mosque incident.  The New York Times called the findings "appalling" and also analysed the data as showing a very high level of distrust of Muslim-Americans and robust disapproval of the [[Park51]] Mosque proposal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Opinion {{!}} Mistrust and the Mosque (Published 2010) |work=The New York Times |date=3 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116032827/https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/03/opinion/03fri1.html?_r=0 |archive-date=2017-11-16 |url-status=live |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/03/opinion/03fri1.html?_r=0}}</ref> ''[[The New Republic]]'' stated that it does not trust the poll carried out by the New York Times and that the figures would be higher than 33%. They further claimed that New York residents are tolerant and if the figures were 33% in New York then "non-New Yorker fellow citizens are far more deeply biased and warped than the Gotham locals".<ref>[https://newrepublic.com/article/77475/the-new-york-times-laments-sadly-wary-misunderstanding-muslim-americans-really-it-sadly-w The New York Times Laments "A Sadly Wary Misunderstanding of Muslim-Americans." But Really Is It "Sadly Wary" Or A "Misunderstanding" At All?]</ref>

==Regions==

===Central Asia===
*85% of interviewed Muslims think that homosexuality is morally wrong. 85% think that sex outside of marriage is morally wrong. 61% think that abortion is morally wrong. 38% think that western pop culture harms morality. 12% favor enshrining Sharia. Among these, 62% want religious judges to oversee family law; 38% want severe corporal punishments for criminals; 16% want to execute those who leave Islam.<ref name="PEW2013">{{cite book |editor-first=Sandra |editor-last=Stence |year=2013 |others=Research: Alan Cooperman, Neha Sahgal, Jessica Hamar Martinez, et al. |title=The World's Muslims: Religion, Politics and Society |publisher=The Pew Forum on Religion & Public Life |url=http://www.pewforum.org/files/2013/04/worlds-muslims-religion-politics-society-full-report.pdf |access-date=5 October 2016 |archive-date=30 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030223449/http://www.pewforum.org/files/2013/04/worlds-muslims-religion-politics-society-full-report.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Middle East-North Africa===
*93% of interviewed Muslims think that homosexuality is morally wrong. 94% think that sex outside of marriage is morally wrong. 72% think that abortion is morally wrong. 51% think that western pop culture harms morality. 74% favor enshrining Sharia. Among these, 78% want religious judges to oversee family law; 57% want severe corporal punishments for criminals; 56% want to execute those who leave Islam.<ref name="PEW2013" />

===South Asia===
*79% of interviewed Muslims think that homosexuality is morally wrong. 87% think that sex outside of marriage is morally wrong. 64% think that abortion is morally wrong. 59% think that western pop culture harms morality. 84% favor enshrining Sharia. Among these, 78% want religious judges to oversee family law; 81% want severe corporal punishments for criminals; 76% want to execute those who leave Islam.<ref name="PEW2013" />

===Southeast Asia===
*95% of interviewed Muslims think that homosexuality is morally wrong. 94% think that sex outside of marriage is morally wrong. 93% think that abortion is morally wrong. 51% think that western pop culture harms morality. 77% favor enshrining Sharia. Among these, 84% want religious judges to oversee family law; 46% want severe corporal punishments for criminals; 27% want to execute those who leave Islam.<ref name="PEW2013" />

===Southern-Eastern Europe===
*83% of interviewed Muslims think that homosexuality is morally wrong. 67% think that sex outside of marriage is morally wrong. 71% think that abortion is morally wrong. 35% think that western pop culture harms morality. 18% favor enshrining Sharia. Among these, 41% want religious judges to oversee family law; 36% want severe corporal punishments for criminals; 13% want to execute those who leave Islam.<ref name="PEW2013" />

===Sub-Saharan Africa===
*91% of interviewed Muslims think that homosexuality is morally wrong. 78% think that sex outside of marriage is morally wrong. 88% think that abortion is morally wrong. 65% think that western pop culture harms morality. 64% favor enshrining Sharia.<ref name="PEW2013" />
